name: What are the best ETL Tools and how they help businesses?
summary: To derive actionable insights from their business data organizations resort to ETL tools. In this blog we will present the list of best ETL tools for your business needs.
author: datachannel-research
content:
Every organization has an enormous amount of data in their systems, with more and more adding to it every day. Most organizations fail to extract potential out of their data, and all relevant information remains stuck in silos.

To cover the inefficiency gap and survive in the ever-changing data landscape, organizations must back their [data pipelines](https://datachannel.co/blogs/build-vs-buy-data-pipelines/) with the best ETL tools.

[ETL tools](https://datachannel.co/blogs/what-is-etl-and-how-the-etl-process-works/) are of great importance when it comes to extracting data from several sources and making it compatible before it is loaded into a centralized repository. Here are some of the best ETL tools you can pick to make your data integration process flawless.

## The Best ETL Tools that make the task of data integration easier

### DataChannel

DataChannel brings you a comprehensive and robust data integration solution that lets you [integrate data from multiple sources](https://datachannel.co/blogs/integrate-multiple-api-data-from-multiple-sources-into-one-place/) to a data warehouse. The platform is backed with tried and tested pre-built models that help you sync all your historical & current data present in both cloud and on-premise platforms.

Being a no-code data platform, DataChannel helps you transfer all your crucial data to the desired warehouse and visualize it in any BI tool. With this solution, you can enrich your data and make it analysis-ready without writing a single code.

[DataChannel](https://datachannel.co/) can be your perfect companion when it comes to growing and nurturing your business in the competitive data-driven industry.

Pros:

-   Offers you all the customization you need
-   Help you manage data across multiple digital marketing channels
-   Provide marketing integrations at a granular level
-   Allow you to view ad creatives from within the dashboard
-   Centralize all your data in real-time
-   Accelerate the reporting process

[

![DataChannel Reverse ETL to activate your data](/images/cms/blogs/blogcta-10-1--33fe6e.png)

](https://console.datachannel.co/register)

### Xplenty

Xplenty is a cloud-based ETL and ELT (Extract, Load, and Transform) platform that helps you combine data from multiple sources. It’s easy-to-understand and intuitive visual interface helps users build robust data pipelines between multiple sources and destinations.

Pros:

-   Easy to navigate GUI
-   Manage & filter the data before it goes to the data destination
-   Offer [API connectors](https://datachannel.co/blogs/integrate-multiple-api-data-from-multiple-sources-into-one-place/) to pull data from different sources
-   Transform data

Cons:

-   Operational errors may occur
-   Error messages are not always descriptive
-   Lack of real-time data synchronization capabilities
-   No on-premise solution

### Talend

Talend is an [open-source ETL data integration](https://datachannel.co/blogs/etl-data-integration-all-you-need-to-know/) tool that offers compatibility with both on-cloud and on-premise data sources. It offers hundreds of pre-built integrations that make the task of data consolidation easier.

The tool can integrate well with most of the well-known cloud service providers, such as [Microsoft Azure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Azure) and [Google Cloud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Cloud_Platform).

Pros:

-   Compatible with different formats like JSON, XML, and CSV.
-   Works well with multiple data sources.
-   Collects data from social media platforms like Facebook and Twitter.
-   Offer real-time integration of data.

Cons:

-   For high-level customization, expertise in JAVA is required
-   Scheduling and automation is basic.

[

![DataChannel Reverse ETL to activate your data](/images/cms/blogs/blogcta-11-1--1b2bab.png)

](https://datachannel.co/blogs/reverse-etl-definitive-guide/)

### Improvado

Improvado is a cloud-based marketing data integration tool that combines multiple data sources into a single virtual database. It pulls data from complex silos and presents it on multiple dashboards in real-time. With this tool, you get the choice to view your data in its dashboard or push the same into a preferred [data warehouse](https://datachannel.co/blogs/introduction-to-data-warehousing/).

Pros:

-   Allows comparison between cross-channel metrics to help you make the right decisions
-   Provide raw and mapped data as required
-   Compatible with BI tools, like Looker and Tableau

Cons:

-   Some features may be a bit complicated
-   Sometimes, you have to go back and forth with the support representatives to get your dashboards & reports visualized

### Alooma

Alooma is a data integration platform with excellent ETL capabilities. The tool helps you build a powerful data pipeline that will focus on maintaining data quality and eliminating every error, even at the granular level. It also assists you with [data migration](https://datachannel.co/blogs/plan-a-successful-data-migration-strategy/) to any data warehouse of your choice. For organizations working at a large scale, Alooma can be an option to consider.

Pros:

-   Works well with multiple data sources
-   Simplifies the task of analyzing all data sources
-   Can replicate all popular databases
-   Allow monitoring data in real-time
-   Detects the schema of the database on its own

Cons:

-   It takes time for new users to understand its GUI
-   Debugging module is a little complex in comparison to other options available

### Domo

Domo offers a [cloud-based data integration solution](https://datachannel.co/blogs/data-integration-everything-you-need-to-know/) that helps you bring all your data in one place. The tool collects data from various sources and displays the same using an interactive format. Its user-friendly interface makes it easier for you to derive crucial business insights to power up your decision-making process. With this solution at your end, making time-sensitive decisions no longer remains a far-fetched task.

Pros:

-   Data transmission can be processed without a lot of bandwidth.
-   An efficient operating system that helps you make real-time decisions.
-   Uses machine learning that facilitate the making of smart decisions for business growth.

Cons:

-   Designed keeping corporate users in mind, individuals may get confused with the numerous options available.
-   It’s a bit complicated to manage databases.

### AWS Glue

AWS Glue, a popular Cloud ETL tool by Amazon, has made its way to help organizations with big data analytics. The tool has simplified the [ETL process](https://datachannel.co/blogs/what-is-etl-and-how-the-etl-process-works/), and its exceptional support with other AWS ecosystem applications makes it a go-to option.

Being a serverless data integration service, the tool helps you discover, prepare, and consolidate data for analytics, machine learning, and application development.

Pros:

-   Allows deployment of applications within minutes
-   A scalable solution that grows with your requirements
-   Connects with non-standardized SQL data sources

Cons:

-   Like other cloud services, AWS is also bound to general computing glitches.
-   AWS Paid technical support may push you to go for other options

## But how can one know which ETL tool will fit best into their organizational needs?

Choosing the right ETL tool for your business doesn’t work on the concept of one size fits all. Every tool has a few distinctive features, and therefore identifying which tool will work best for your business is crucial.

Before starting your search for the best ETL tool, understand the complexity of your [data integration process](https://datachannel.co/blogs/data-integration-everything-you-need-to-know/) and consult with analysts.

With the right ETL tool by your side, you can hit deadlines for all your projects and turn into a truly data-driven organization.
